current_text: Chaff trodden flat across the boards, and the corner sacks are open along their bottom seams. Something behind the last row is breathing.
Each notch is a flood, with its year cut underneath. The oldest years run back past the village's first headman, and the shelf clears the highest notch by a hand.
The rail carries on east from here. A pair of sparrows lift off the top bar and settle again three posts down.
The top rail is rubbed bare along one stretch, and it gives a dry knock when you set a hand on it.
A low rail on the west boundary of the rows. Bindweed has taken the near post to the top and stopped there.

The stone stands at the middle of the village with a spiral cut into its face, softened by weather. Attunement works like this: show a door the right stone and the door learns the place, and can open onto it ever after. The grass around its base is worn down to bare dirt.
After dark the field's edge has eyes in it, low to the ground and catching the light. Look straight at them and they go out. They are back as soon as your eye moves off.
[Basic Repair] — You cut boards to the span and lay them across the stringers. The walk takes your weight from one end to the other.
The first sack moves. Your back has nothing for the eleven behind it. Shifting a stack like that takes strength you have not learned yet.
Grain sacks off a dray at the bank head, a dozen of them on the boards. Two men stand looking at the stack with their hands on their hips.
The dray stands empty and the shed is stacked to the door. The bank head has no more work in it until tomorrow.
Hazel hurdles cut and stacked against the pen rail, as many again as the fold already has standing.
The third lamb, lying apart from the other two with the bad foreleg held up off the straw.
Two bars and a post. The tilled rows start a stride past it.
You put the spoon in and take it out again. The water goes on turning at its own pace, and nothing in the pot has changed.
The cauldron is lit and the water is already moving. Stir it properly and there is a remedy in it.
A struck match does nothing to the wicks at this door. They will only take a light you make yourself.
Root and briar have grown into a single knot at the middle of the standing stones. The strands are all pulled tight, each toward whichever stone stands closest.
[Observe] — Look at it squarely and the knot resolves into a price, tied off and unpaid. You pay it where you stand, and the pull goes out of the briar all across the hollow.
Bramble twisted into a running loop at ankle height — a snare, and the knot in it is one your hands already know.
At the hollow's west edge stands a second house, smaller than the cottage, with half its roof fallen in. The door is open on the dark, and shallow marks cross the lintel in a line worn nearly smooth.
A tree grown out sideways over the path. You go under it with your head down.
A palm of grey stone lying flat on the shelf, one edge set square to the front. The rest of the shelf runs crooked.

[Detect Magic] — What is left here is one link of a boundary that once closed around the whole thicket. Its pull still faces inward, along the exact line the deer refuse to cross. It was drawn to keep something in; it stopped doing that a very long time ago.
The top shelf holds a row of stoppered jars with nothing left readable on the labels.
The latch is on the inside of the shutter, and the hut was shut when you came to it. Dust lies along the sill, unbroken.
